text: nice can u add in a button or preview or something that will place the player model against the model being made for scale
resolution: Added a scale-reference 'player ghost' to the Studio mesh editor so the user can size a model against a real person. A new 'scale' toggle in the viewport's top-left overlay mounts THE in-game player figure (same seed) standing on the grid just past the model's bounding radius, with feet at y=0 and the height readout (1.65 m collider, RULED R4) on the button. It reuses the proven Embodied render path verbatim — GAME_FIGURE.generateFace + buildPartRender + buildRigFrame, rendered via FigureMeshes (intern=true, so the static figure uses the retained geometry buffer and never competes for the sculpt DYN slots) plus CharacterCaptures for the face/skin textures, under a unique 'studio-scale' cartKey so its captures don't collide with /test's player. The figure is built once (useMemo) and placed via a frame.radius-derived offset; the toggle is twig hot-state (studio:showScale). Files: editors/model/Studio.tsx (imports GAME_FIGURE + figure/render + world/scale; new SCALE_FIGURE_SEED/CART_KEY consts, scaleFigureGapMeters tunable, showScale state, scaleFigure memo, Scene3D figure block, toggle button). Verified by bundling the full hmsc-int cart through esbuild with the real ship alias set: exit 0, no errors. NOT committed: editors/model/ is entirely untracked in this tree (another lane's uncommitted work), so a clean own-work-only commit isn't possible; flagged to the user.
